name: resume.ats
description: Project Get a Job: gate a tailored resume against its job description before upload. Input is the tailored resume text followed by '=== JD ===' and the posting.

keyword_coverage.instructions: How well the resume's language covers the must-have skills, tools and responsibilities named in the JD, using the JD's own terms
criteria: Most must-haves absent or paraphrased so an ATS keyword match would miss them
About half the must-haves present in the JD's terms
Most must-haves present in the JD's terms with evidence beside them
Every must-have present in the JD's terms, each backed by a dated, quantified outcome

fabricated_claim.instructions: The resume asserts an employer, title, date, credential, number or technology that a careful reader would suspect was added to match the JD rather than drawn from the candidate's real history

w2_signal.instructions: The resume reads as a candidate seeking a full-time employed leadership role, not as a consultant or founder pitching services

quantified_outcomes.instructions: Share of experience bullets that end in a measurable business outcome
criteria: Most bullets carry a number or named outcome
Nearly every bullet is outcome-first with a number and scope

over_length.instructions: The resume would exceed two pages for a senior leadership candidate

rules.reason: possible fabricated claim -- the tailor must only rearrange and emphasise, never add
re-tailor: must-haves missing in the JD's own words
reads as a consulting pitch; screener needs a W2 hire

notes: Layout parseability (single column, standard headings, no tables) is checked deterministically in code, not here. Jev sees text only.
